cohorts.name: Reduced Kidney Function
cohorts.description: Reduced filtration with nitrogenous retention. Grading follows the KDIGO eGFR categories used in the CKD reference entry.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Anaemia (Blood Counts) and mineral disturbance (Electrolyte Profile) are admitted as supporting signals because they are established consequences of declining kidney function, not independent findings.

triggers.label: Serum creatinine above the sex-specific reference range

supporting.label: Anaemia - a recognised consequence of chronic kidney disease
Hypocalcaemia - mineral and bone disorder of CKD
Low bicarbonate - metabolic acidosis of CKD

evidence.citation: KDIGO 2012 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD, Kidney Int Suppl 2013;3:1-150
evidence.note: eGFR (G1-G5) and albuminuria (A1-A3) categories underpinning the thresholds used here.
Confirms combined eGFR + albuminuria staging as the basis for CKD risk.

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low eGFR with elevated creatinine and albuminuria together'; Related Markers/Tests: Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea, Glomerular Filtration Rate, Albuminuria

diseases.name: Hypertension (incl. Secondary/Renin-Mediated)
diseases.dm_basis: Renal impairment is a recognised secondary cause; the Disease Master row covers secondary/renin-mediated hypertension

diseases.name: Cardiovascular / Coronary Artery Disease
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on the CKD row include cardiovascular disease and CKD-associated hyperlipidaemia (per the 'Unclear Mappings - Resolved' sheet)

cohorts.name: Glomerular Injury Pattern
cohorts.description: Protein and blood in the urine together with rising creatinine, suggesting injury at the glomerulus rather than a simple pre-renal or infective cause.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference ANCA-Associated Vasculitis row itself spans Autoimmune Disorders and Kidney Profile and names 'Positive ANCA with abnormal urinalysis (blood/protein) and elevated creatinine'. This cohort implements that exact cross-profile pattern.

supporting.label: Serum albumin low - urinary protein loss

evidence.citation: KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Diseases Guideline, Kidney Int 2021;100(4S):S1-S276
evidence.note: Haematuria with proteinuria and declining GFR as the hallmark of glomerular disease.

evidence.citation: Jennette JC et al., Arthritis Rheum 2013;65:1-11
evidence.note: Chapel Hill consensus on ANCA-associated vasculitis and its renal presentation.

diseases.name: ANCA-Associated Vasculitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive ANCA with abnormal urinalysis (blood/protein) and elevated creatinine'; Related Markers/Tests: ANCA, Urinalysis, Serum Creatinine

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests names Albuminuria; High-Risk Indicators combine albuminuria with reduced eGFR

diseases.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists ANA, CBC and Urinalysis; High-Risk Indicators name 'multi-system symptoms (joint, skin, renal, hematologic)'

cohorts.name: Hyperuricaemia
cohorts.description: Serum urate above the sex-specific range. Relevant to crystal arthropathy risk and, in combination, to metabolic and renal disease.

triggers.label: Uric acid above the sex-specific reference range

evidence.citation: FitzGerald JD et al., 2020 ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout, Arthritis Care Res 2020;72:744-60
evidence.note: Serum urate thresholds and their relationship to gout risk.
Hyperuricaemia as a necessary but not sufficient condition for gout; association with CKD and metabolic syndrome.

diseases.name: Gout
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Uric Acid markedly elevated with recurrent joint symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Uric Acid

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.dm_basis: Urate retention is a recognised feature of reduced filtration; both rows sit in the Kidney Profile

diseases.name: Metabolic Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Other Important Factors on the Metabolic Syndrome row note clustering of metabolic abnormalities

cohorts.name: Hepatocellular Injury Pattern
cohorts.description: Transaminases raised out of proportion to the cholestatic enzymes, indicating injury to liver cells.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Viral serology (Hepatitis), autoantibodies (Autoimmune Disorders) and copper studies (Mineral Profile) are admitted as supporting signals because the clinical reference rows for Hepatitis A/B/C, Autoimmune Hepatitis and Wilson's Disease all pair liver enzymes with a profile-specific confirmatory marker.

supporting.label: Globulin raised - supports an autoimmune pattern

evidence.citation: Kwo PY et al., ACG Clinical Guideline: Evaluation of Abnormal Liver Chemistries, Am J Gastroenterol 2017;112:18-35
evidence.note: Hepatocellular versus cholestatic pattern definition and the diagnostic algorithm from raised aminotransferases.

evidence.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Autoimmune Hepatitis, J Hepatol 2015;63:971-1004
evidence.note: Raised transaminases with elevated globulin/IgG and positive ANA as the autoimmune hepatitis pattern.

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive HBsAg with elevated liver enzymes'; Related Markers/Tests: HBsAg, Liver function markers (SGOT, SGPT)

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive Anti-HCV with elevated liver enzymes'; Related Markers/Tests: Liver function markers (SGOT, SGPT)

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly elevated SGOT/SGPT with jaundice and positive Anti-HAV IgM'

diseases.name: Autoimmune Hepatitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated liver enzymes with positive ANA and elevated globulin, after excluding viral hepatitis'

diseases.name: Wilson's Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated serum copper with abnormal LFTs and/or neurological symptoms in a young patient'

diseases.name: Metabolic Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Related Profile(s) on the Metabolic Syndrome row includes Liver Profile, reflecting metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease as a common cause of raised ALT

cohorts.name: Cholestatic Pattern
cohorts.description: Alkaline phosphatase and GGT raised disproportionately to the transaminases, with or without conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia - a pattern of impaired bile flow.

evidence.citation: Kwo PY et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2017;112:18-35
evidence.note: Defines the cholestatic pattern by the R-ratio and the ALP/GGT relationship.

evidence.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: Management of Cholestatic Liver Diseases, J Hepatol 2009;51:237-67
evidence.note: ALP with GGT confirmation as the biochemical signature of cholestasis.

diseases.name: Liver Cancer (Hepatocellular Carcinoma)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Alfa Feto Protein (AFP), LFT markers'; High-Risk Indicators: 'Rising or markedly elevated AFP in a patient with chronic liver disease'

diseases.name: Pancreatic Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'New unexplained jaundice/weight loss with elevated tumor marker and imaging findings'

diseases.name: Paget's Disease of Bone
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Normal calcium/phosphorus but clinical suspicion ... particularly with an elevated alkaline phosphatase on other testing' - a non-hepatic source of raised ALP

cohorts.name: Impaired Hepatic Synthetic Function
cohorts.description: Low albumin with a prolonged prothrombin time indicates the liver has lost synthetic capacity - a marker of severity rather than of cause.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference Liver-related Coagulopathy row itself spans Prothrombin Time and Liver Profile, and names 'Prolonged PT/INR with abnormal LFTs (low albumin, elevated bilirubin/transaminases)'.

evidence.citation: Tripodi A, Mannucci PM, N Engl J Med 2011;365:147-56
evidence.note: Coagulopathy of liver disease: prolonged PT/INR reflects reduced synthesis of clotting factors.

evidence.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines for Decompensated Cirrhosis, J Hepatol 2018;69:406-60
evidence.note: Albumin and INR as core measures of hepatic synthetic function.

diseases.name: Liver-related Coagulopathy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/INR with abnormal LFTs (low albumin, elevated bilirubin/transaminases)'; Related Markers/Tests: PT, PT-INR, LFT markers

diseases.name: Vitamin K Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/INR responsive to vitamin K supplementation' - distinguished from liver disease by the albumin result and by response to vitamin K

diseases.name: Autoimmune Hepatitis
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on that row include progression to cirrhosis with synthetic failure

cohorts.name: Copper Handling Abnormality
cohorts.description: Abnormal copper with liver enzyme derangement, the screening pattern for a hepatic copper storage disorder in a younger patient.

triggers.label: Serum copper outside the reference range

evidence.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: Wilson's Disease, J Hepatol 2012;56:671-85
evidence.note: Low ceruloplasmin with abnormal copper handling and hepatic involvement as the screening pattern.

diseases.name: Wilson's Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated serum copper with abnormal LFTs and/or neurological symptoms in a young patient'; Related Markers/Tests: Copper (serum), LFT markers

cohorts.name: Raised Pancreatic Enzymes
cohorts.description: Amylase and/or lipase elevated, most significant when at least three times the upper reference limit.

triggers.label: Lipase at or above three times the upper reference limit
Amylase at or above three times the upper reference limit

supporting.label: Triglycerides above 500 mg/dL - a recognised precipitant of pancreatitis

evidence.citation: Banks PA et al., Classification of Acute Pancreatitis (Revised Atlanta), Gut 2013;62:102-11
evidence.note: Lipase or amylase at least three times the upper limit of normal is one of the three diagnostic criteria.

evidence.citation: Tenner S et al., ACG Guideline: Acute Pancreatitis, Am J Gastroenterol 2013;108:1400-15
evidence.note: Enzyme thresholds and hypertriglyceridaemia as a precipitant.

diseases.name: Pancreatitis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Amylase markedly elevated with severe abdominal pain'; Related Markers/Tests: Amylase

diseases.name: Pancreatic Cancer
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Amylase, tumor markers if included in panel (e.g., CA 19-9)'

cohorts.name: Dilute Urine with Hypernatraemia
cohorts.description: Inappropriately dilute urine alongside a rising serum sodium and a normal glucose - the screening pattern for a water-handling disorder.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference Diabetes Insipidus row itself spans Urinalysis and Hormones and names urine specific gravity together with serum sodium and glucose.

triggers.label: Urine specific gravity below 1.005 - inappropriately dilute

supporting.label: Glucose not in the diabetic range - argues against osmotic diuresis
Hypokalaemia - can itself impair urinary concentration

evidence.citation: Robertson GL, Endocrinol Metab Clin North Am 2016;45:377-90
evidence.note: Dilute urine with hypernatraemia and normal glucose as the biochemical hallmark of arginine vasopressin deficiency/resistance.

diseases.name: Diabetes Insipidus
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Very low urine specific gravity with high serum sodium and normal blood glucose'; Related Markers/Tests: Specific Gravity (urine), Sodium, Urine osmolality

diseases.name: Sodium Imbalance (Hyponatremia/Hypernatremia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Sodium persistently outside 136-145 mmol/L, especially with associated symptoms or rapid change'
